newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks close up but off day's high.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks close up but off day's high.

text.p: Jakarta stocks closed up but off a new all-time on Monday, pulled up by a spurt of late buying of blue chips after the market earlier underwent a brief consolidation period, brokers said.

Brokers said mid-afternoon profit-taking in was due to consolidation. The market had also eased because the country's latest economic deregulation package, expected to provide fresh leads, was not unveiled during trading hours.
The Composite Index closed up 1.41 points, or 0.19 percent, at 738.01 points after hitting a new all-time-high of 739.83 points during the day.
The government unveiled its latest deregulation package, cutting tariffs on 1,600 items.
Brokers and analysts expected it would boost market sentiment on Tuesday and spur fresh buying in counters which would benefit from the package.

"I think market still needs some time to digests the package and its impact on certain sectors. But in general it should give positive sentiment on Indonesian economy," a senior analyst with a Hongkong-based securities firm said.
He attributed the sharp rise in car maker Astra International to expectations that tariff cuts would be of benefit to the company.
Blue chips such as HM Sampoerna, Astra International, Indosat and Indocement were among targets for buyers, brokers said.

Chemical firm Eterindo Wahana topped the active list with some 52 million shares changing hands, rising 25 rupiah to 2,200 rupiah on speculation that the firm will benefit from the deregulation package, brokers said.
Property firms including Surya Semesta Internusa, Mas Murni Indonesia, Pakuwon Jati and Jababeka were among active stocks on similar expectation, brokers said.

"The news on Neraca daily this morning that government might limit the loans to property developers had sparked speculation of which property firms will benefit or will loose from the deregulations," an analyst said.
Central Bank Governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said the government would limit loans to property developers for land purchases.
